assertions.title: CAS refcount store crash recovery

steps.expected: Test increments refcount x5, persists (fsync), simulates crash by dropping store, reopens, and verifies refcount is exactly 5
steps.observed: Test does exactly this: opens store, incr x5 on hash of b'crash recovery persist', calls persist() (which does atomic write+fsync+rename), drops store (simulating kill), reopens, asserts refcount == 5. Correctly exercises the 'persisted via fsync before ack' requirement.

steps.expected: Test increments refcount x3 WITHOUT calling persist, drops store (simulating crash before fsync), reopens, and verifies refcount <= 3 (lost increments acceptable, phantom counts not)
steps.observed: Test does exactly this: first session persists a different hash to create the sidecar file, second session increments h x3 in-memory without persist, drops without fsync, third session reopens and asserts refcount(h) <= 3. The comment explicitly states 'phantom refcounts after crash-not-fsynced'. Correctly exercises the 'no phantom refcount' requirement.

steps.expected: persist() writes to temp file, fsyncs, then atomically renames to refs.json. This ensures crash before rename loses the write (no phantom), crash after rename preserves it.
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: persist() serializes to JSON, creates uniquely-named temp file, BufWriter write_all + flush + fsync_file, then fs::rename (atomic on same filesystem), plus best-effort dir fsync. This is the correct write-barrier pattern.

steps.expected: open() reads sidecar if exists, uses unwrap_or_default() for corrupt/missing file (starts empty), ensuring crash-tolerant recovery
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: serde_json::from_slice(&data).unwrap_or_default() gracefully handles corrupt JSON by returning empty map. Missing file returns empty HashMap. Both paths produce a clean empty store on corrupt/missing sidecar.

sourceFiles: src/storage/cas/refs.rs lines 101-117 (open with crash recovery), lines 168-202 (persist with atomic write+fsync+rename)
evidence.testResult: not executed (no shell tool available); determined pass by source code analysis
evidence.codeAnalysisNotes: Both tests correctly exercise the two crash-recovery scenarios required by VAL-CAS-016. The persist-then-crash test verifies no refcount lost. The no-persist-then-crash test verifies no phantom refcount. Implementation uses atomic temp-file+fsync+rename write barrier.

assertions.title: CAS refcount underflow safety

steps.expected: Test decrements a blob with refcount 0 (never incremented) and verifies it returns CasError::RefcountUnderflow, never going negative
steps.observed: Test creates a hash via blob_hash(b'underflow test'), calls store.decr(&h) on a store where h was never incr'd (refcount 0), asserts unwrap_err() matches CasError::RefcountUnderflow. Correctly exercises the underflow-at-zero requirement.

steps.action: Read test_refcount_two_decrs_from_one in refs_test.rs (lines 54-62) as additional coverage
steps.expected: Test increments once, decrements to 0, then decrements again at 0 and verifies underflow error
steps.observed: Test increments h once (refcount=1), decrements to 0, then attempts second decr which must return RefcountUnderflow. This covers the sequential decrement scenario where refcount reaches 0 then is decremented again.

steps.expected: decr() checks if current count is 0 before decrementing; if 0, returns Err(CasError::RefcountUnderflow) without modifying the count
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: decr() uses entry().or_insert(0), checks if *entry == 0, returns Err(CasError::RefcountUnderflow) if so. Only decrements if > 0. The count can never go negative because the subtraction is guarded by the zero check.

evidence.testResult: not executed (no shell tool available); determined pass by source code analysis
evidence.codeAnalysisNotes: The underflow guard is a simple zero-check before subtraction. The test covers both the never-incremented case (refcount 0 from the start) and the decremented-to-zero-then-decrement-again case. Both produce RefcountUnderflow.

assertions.title: CAS blob content-addressing identifies duplicates across generations

steps.expected: Test puts identical content twice into the same CAS store, verifies both puts return the same hash, and verifies only one blob is stored on disk (blob_count == 1)
steps.observed: Test puts b'shared content across conceptual generations' twice, asserts h1 == h2 ('identical content -> identical hash'), asserts store.blob_count() == 1 ('one blob on disk, not two'). Correctly exercises the cross-generation dedup requirement.

steps.expected: blob_hash uses blake3::hash(payload) -- a pure content hash. Identical payloads always produce identical hashes regardless of when or where they are stored.
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: blob_hash(payload) returns blake3::hash(payload).into(). Blake3 is deterministic -- same bytes always produce the same 32-byte digest. This is the foundation of content-addressed dedup.

steps.expected: put() checks if final_path.exists() before writing. If blob already exists, returns early with the same hash (no-op). This prevents storing two copies.
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: put() computes hash, checks if final_path.exists(), and if so returns Ok(hash) immediately without writing. The second put of identical content is a complete no-op at the storage layer. blob_count() walks the directory tree and counts actual blob files, confirming only one exists.

steps.expected: Additional test verifies that two separate CAS stores produce identical hashes for the same payload
steps.observed: test_hash_determinism_cross_store opens two stores in different tempdirs, puts the same payloads in each, and asserts hashes match (ha == hb). This confirms content-addressing is deterministic across store instances (conceptually, across generations).

evidence.codeAnalysisNotes: Content-addressing via blake3 ensures identical content always maps to the same hash. The put() method's exists-check prevents duplicate storage. The test verifies both the hash equality and the single-blob-on-disk invariant.

assertions.title: CAS store opens on empty directory

steps.expected: Test opens CasStore on a nonexistent nested path, verifies no error, verifies staging directory is created, verifies first put works, and verifies get on unknown hash returns NotFound (not crash/corrupt error)
steps.observed: Test creates path nested/cas under a tempdir (which doesn't exist yet), calls CasStore::open(&root), expects success. Asserts root.join(STAGING_DIR).exists(). Puts b'first' and gets it back successfully. Then gets an unknown hash and asserts CasError::NotFound. Correctly exercises all first-run requirements.

steps.expected: open() calls fs::create_dir_all on root and staging dir, then opens JsonSidecarStore. create_dir_all creates all missing parent directories. No error on empty/nonexistent path.
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: open() calls fs::create_dir_all(&root) then fs::create_dir_all(root.join(STAGING_DIR)), then JsonSidecarStore::open(&root). create_dir_all is idempotent and creates all intermediate directories. JsonSidecarStore::open checks if sidecar exists; if not, starts with empty HashMap. No spurious 'corrupt' errors possible.

steps.action: Verify JsonSidecarStore::open() handles missing sidecar (refs.rs lines 101-117)
steps.expected: If refs.json does not exist, store initializes with empty HashMap. No error.
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: if sidecar_path.exists() is false, counts = HashMap::new(). Returns Ok(JsonSidecarStore { counts, sidecar_path }). Clean first-run initialization.

steps.action: Verify get() returns NotFound for unknown hash (mod.rs lines 143-151)
steps.expected: get() checks if blob path exists; if not, returns CasError::NotFound (not a corrupt error or panic)
steps.observed: Implementation confirmed: get() checks if path.exists(), returns Err(CasError::NotFound) if not. No panic, no corrupt error.
